passage:
A supermarket tested labels showing the estimated carbon footprint of some foods. The labels helped shoppers compare products beyond price.
Some people found them useful. Others said the numbers were confusing. A store worker explained that the label was not meant to make every decision for customers. It was meant to give one more piece of information.
A student used the labels for a school project. She learned that food choices are connected to farming, transport, storage, and waste.
The label did not tell a complete story, but it started a conversation.
Shopping is often treated as a private act. The carbon label showed that it also has public effects.

本文沒有陳述「The Forgotten Public Toilet」；這個選項混入另一個情境的資訊。
